intro.text: This page describes how your authorisation server constructs and sends JWT Auth tokens when calling the API Hub's Consent Manager and Headless Heimdall Auth Server endpoints. See Application Layer Authentication for an overview of all available methods and when to select JWT Auth.

Sending JWT Auth from the LFI to the API Hub is optional even when JWT Auth is selected. It is configured separately from the API Hub → LFI direction — indicate your preference on the onboarding Service Desk ticket.

When your authorisation server calls API Hub endpoints (Consent Manager or Headless Heimdall Auth Server), you MUST construct a JWT Auth token and include it as a Bearer token in the Authorization HTTP header. The request MUST also be made over mutual TLS — see Configuring Outbound mTLS.

sections.heading: Set up the C3-hh-cm-client application
sections.category: Publishing signing keys on a JWKS

items: Create an Application in your Trust Framework Organisation labelled C3-hh-cm-client.
Create both the C3 transport client certificate and Sig4 signing certificate in this Application using the code snippets provided in the Trust Framework.
The Trust Framework will create a unique kid and host the JWKS.
When publishing a new key, wait 10 minutes before issuing a message signed with that key. This allows the receiver's JWKS cache to refresh.
Ensure the machine generating the signature uses NTP to synchronise its clock.
Construct the JWT header and payload as specified in the Claims Reference below.
Sign the JWT using the PS256 algorithm with a private signing key from the C3-hh-cm-client application.
Include the JWT as a Bearer token in the Authorization HTTP header.

The HTTPS request MUST be made over mutual TLS. The C3 client certificate MUST be used to initiate the mTLS session, and MUST have a DN and OU that match the values placed in the JWT signature claims.

rows: The key ID of the keypair used to sign the message, as published on the JWKS.
Other means of identifying the key (e.g. x5c, x5u ) are not supported.
The organisation O value from the TLS certificate Subject used in the transport layer.
For a certificate with Subject CN=ABC, OU=XYZ, O=Acme Bank, C=AE, this would be Acme Bank.
The organisation unit OU value from the TLS certificate Subject used in the transport layer.
For the same certificate, this would be XYZ.
Identifier for the party receiving the JWT.
This MUST be set to the PROVIDER_ID specified during configuration.
Time when the JWT will expire, in UTC seconds since epoch.
Recommended expiry: 10–30 seconds. When validating, allow for a 10-second clock skew. The JWT is invalid if the current time is greater than this value.
Time when the JWT was issued, in UTC seconds since epoch.
When validating, allow for a 10-second clock skew. The JWT is invalid if the current time is less than this value.
Time before which the JWT is invalid, in UTC seconds since epoch.
When validating, allow for a 10-second clock skew. The JWT is invalid if the current time is less than this value (when specified).
A unique identifier for the JWT.
Recommended: populate with a UUIDv4 to increase entropy.
